refuters.argument:
Not refuted. The Lean `P D := reMap (phi (T.toTG (lmF D)))` is the coefficientwise real part of the Gaussian evaluation φ(F_D) with φ(l)=i·a, φ(m)=(−i)·z (LinkLaurentRing.lean:1288-1290, phi_l/phi_m at 1305-1321), which is exactly eq. lp:gaussian (sm-3:1067-1069). I confirmed the substitution is the correct one rather than merely sign-plausible: pushing lp:source-skein through φ gives a·P₊ − a⁻¹·P₋ = z·P₀ (lp:skein) and φ(μ) = (a − a⁻¹)z⁻¹ = δ, so the Lean evaluation reproduces both printed lp:core clauses.

Attack 1 (a diagram with Re φ(F_D) ≠ printed P_D): none exists. φ(l^p m^q) = (−1)^q i^{p+q} a^p z^q is real iff p+q is even; μ's monomials have p+q ∈ {0,−2}, and the skein rewrite F₊ = −l⁻²F₋ − l⁻¹m F₀ preserves this parity, so φ(F_D) always lies in R.toRG's image and reMap_toRG (LinkLaurentRing.lean:1098) returns exactly the printed element of R. On every diagram where the printed P_D is meaningful, the two coincide.

Attack 2 (definition needs lp:core): it does not; reMap totalizes P without the descent. The only residue is abstract and pre-lp:core: `P D = 1` unfolds to Re φ(F_D) = 1, which alone does not force Im φ(F_D) = 0 (a hypothetical F_D = 1 + l would satisfy the Lean conclusion but not the printed one). This cannot happen for this row's diagrams: lmF D is pinned to μ⁰ = 1 by LMClauses.underFirst_init (LinkInterfaces.lean) once an UNDER-first basing is exhibited — the printed proof's own route (sm-3:1353-1357) — and it becomes a full equivalence for all D when lp:core's planned field R.toRG (P D) = φ(F_D) is proved. Non-blocking; optionally the bundle could additionally record phi (T.toTG (lmF D)) = 1 or lmF D = 1, though the printed statement is about P_D ∈ R so P D = 1 is the correct target.

Attack 3 (degenerate P D = 1): P is not constant — for a two-component crossing-free diagram lmF D = μ (lmF_crossingFree, c = 2) so P D = δ ≠ 1. UnderFirst B (LinkDiagram.lean:1560-1561) is a strict Prod.Lex comparison of basedRank on the two distinct visits of each crossing; on one circle ranks tie and cyclic offsets differ (visitPt_injective), so it is neither vacuous nor universally true, and nonsingular basepoints exist in any open arc (exists_nonsingular_base pattern). The value 1 arises only via the c = 1 initialization μ^{c−1} = 1 and φ(1) = 1, exactly what the printed lemma licenses. lmF is Classical.choose of the accepted axiom lp_lm; P adds no axioms and no coercion trap (R is an abbrev for Laurent₂ ℤ, so (1 : R) is single (0,0) 1 and reMap 1 = 1).

For the purposes of this row, the definition of P is a faithful rendering of the printed P_D.

(ii) Distinct Lean crossings are distinct double points: `tail_off` (no vertex on a non-incident edge; `incident` = Polygon.lean:60) forces every meeting point of non-adjacent edges to be interior to both edges (this is the layer's own `Generic.crossingPoint_param`, LinkDiagram.lean:434-436, giving 0 < tau < 1), and `no_triple` then forbids a third edge through it; the layer proves exactly this as `Generic.crossingPoint_injective` (:463-464).
